unified-diff.description: A unified patch, either as one text value or as a file manifest whose patch fields Leaf delivers separately on demand.

instructions.producer:
Pipe the exact Git patch, with Git's default `a/` and `b/` prefixes, through this package's producer script into the source:

```bash
git diff <base>...<head> | leaf package run diff patch_manifest.py | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

The script keys each file by its destination path. A file `lf-diff` can't present shows its refusal on the page and reports it to you as the page's error.

calldiff.description: CallDiff's native JSON diff result, including trees, statuses and optional source coordinates.

instructions.producer:
Pipe CallDiff 0.5.0 or newer with `--format json` directly into the source:

```bash
calldiff diff <base> <head> --entry <entry> --format json | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

Keep the native JSON object intact. Locations are included in the structured trees even without `--locs`.

lf-diff.description: A unified patch with per-file navigation and commentable source lines.
lf-diff.x-instructions: Without `source`, write the exact Git patch in the `<pre>` at column 0, HTML-escaped (& before < and >), or entity text in the patch will change silently. Keep Git's file headers and metadata, and make each hunk's `@@` counts match its lines. Keep the leading space on context lines, and write a context line that is only a space as ` ` so HTML parsing keeps it. With `source`, bind a page-owned patch feed or files manifest and leave the `<pre>` empty. Add `collapsed` to start every file closed. Use view="file" beside a separate file navigator to show one file at a time without a second file listing; datum navigation selects and opens its file. Markdown and plain-text files wrap by default; other files scroll sideways. Set `overflow="wrap"` or `overflow="scroll"` to choose one mode for every file in the widget. Textual patches from inline content or available source data reserve their drawn height; leave `data-height` off these. The package author instructions describe initial-height limits for other source forms.
lf-diff.x-example:
diff --git a/feeders/mount.py b/feeders/mount.py
--- a/feeders/mount.py
+++ b/feeders/mount.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def bracket():
-    return "plastic"
+    return "steel"

lf-call-diff.description: A commentable call-tree diff, linked to the `lf-diff` that holds its patch.
lf-call-diff.x-instructions: Set `diff` to the id of the `lf-diff` holding the exact patch. Keep the unchanged items in the tree as landmarks. In a large repository, give each widget one file or entry point. Don't copy the output into markup, add attribute reads as calls, or draw separate before and after diagrams.

lf-worktree-diffs.description: A supplied set of expandable worktree snapshots, with aggregate change totals and independent diff readers.
lf-worktree-diffs.x-instructions: Supply `lf-worktree` members in review order; the collection lists unavailable snapshots apart from its totals.
lf-worktree-diffs.x-example:
Preserve a composer draft while switching threads.

diff --git a/draft.js b/draft.js
--- a/draft.js
+++ b/draft.js
@@ -1 +1 @@
-clearDraft();
+saveDraft();

lf-worktree.description: One worktree snapshot inside lf-worktree-diffs, an expandable row whose summary Leaf writes from its attributes and whose body holds the evidence authored directly inside it.
